task: Fossil fuel dependency index per US state (50 states + DC), 2017
method: Solar: Google Project Sunroof state file read with csv.DictReader (utf-8-sig); dropped the single non-geographic row with state_name=='NULL'; solar_potential_MWh_2017 = yearly_sunlight_kwh_total / 1000 (kWh -> MWh). 51/51 states present.

Generation: streamed US_Energy_Generation_2001-2022.csv (496,774 rows); kept YEAR=='2017' and TYPE OF PRODUCER=='Total Electric Power Industry' (aggregate; sub-producer categories excluded to avoid double counting) and ENERGY SOURCE in {Coal, Natural Gas, Petroleum}; summed GENERATION (Megawatthours) over 12 months per state; mapped 2-letter STATE to full name (dropped 'US-TOTAL').

Price: streamed U.S._Electricity_Prices.csv; kept year=='2017', sectorName=='industrial'; excluded the 11 aggregate entities (U.S. Total + 9 census divisions + 2 Pacific aggregates); annual price = simple mean of the 12 monthly 'price' values (already cents/kWh).

Inner-joined the three sources on full state name (51/51 entities, no missing, no duplicates), computed the index without rounding inputs, sorted alphabetically by state_name, wrote output.csv with the 5 required columns.

validation.notes: DC has only 24 fossil source-month rows (no coal generation); Vermont has the smallest fossil generation (8,940 MWh). Values match an independent line-based recomputation for the spot-checked states.
